output.summary: The referenced LT Verdict analysis is VALID with COMPLETE coverage and a deterministic policy verdict of NO_POLICY. Both the reference window (epoch 1767225600000–1767225720000) and the evaluation window (epoch 1767225720000–1767225960000) report NO_POLICY for business and resource verdicts, meaning no applicable policy rule was evaluated; healthy-looking metrics (0 sampled errors, p95 latency ~236 ms on 7200 overall samples) do not convert NO_POLICY into PASS. Sixteen resource-to-p95-latency correlation pairs were tested in the evaluation window; all dropped the constant 20 requests/s target control (CONSTANT_CONTROL), all report uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, and only pair-14 (resource-14) passed Holm-adjusted selection (adjusted p 0.016) as a correlation candidate with best_lag_ms -10000 and best_lag_rho -0.4872. Clock alignment is not verified by core, and the anomaly diagnostic tested 0 episodes, so lead/lag ordering, load dependence, and stability should not be inferred. Advice preserves the NO_POLICY verdict and recommends clock verification, policy configuration, and load-varying reruns before drawing causal conclusions.

hypotheses.observation: Both the reference and evaluation window policy summaries report business_verdict NO_POLICY, resource_verdict NO_POLICY, and overall verdict NO_POLICY, and the deterministic policy_verdict is NO_POLICY.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The product reports NO_POLICY when no applicable rule exists for the window (no business policy rule and no resource rule with effect: sla); a healthy window or zero sampled errors does not turn NO_POLICY into PASS.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm which business policy rules and resource rules with effect: sla were configured for these windows; if none apply, configure an applicable SLA policy and rerun so the product can evaluate PASS or FAIL.

hypotheses.observation: pair-14 (resource-14 vs response_time_p95_ms) is the only selected correlation headline after Holm correction at alpha 0.05 (holm_adjusted_p_value 0.016, max_p_value 0.001, status SELECTED), with best_lag_ms -10000, best_lag_rho -0.487172887046, raw_rho -0.105232474746, partial_rho -0.105232474746, and is reported as a correlation_candidate finding.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A lagged association between resource-14 and p95 response time in the evaluation window appears strong relative to the 16-hypothesis family; however, the best lag sits at the edge of the tested lag range and its direction cannot be interpreted as causal timing without verified clocks or load variation.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment between metric and resource telemetry first, then inspect the resource-14 series around the evaluation window (mean 0.485131525, slope_per_second 0.0005006 in that window) and rerun with variable load to test whether the association reproduces.

hypotheses.observation: All 16 correlation pairs list controls_requested ["target"], controls_dropped ["target"], controls_used [], and reason CONSTANT_CONTROL; the target series is constant at 20 requests/s with sample_standard_deviation 0 in both windows, and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps is null for every pair.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because the load target was a constant 20 requests/s through the window, the load control could not be used, so partial correlations were computed without controlling for achieved load and no load-sensitivity estimate could be produced.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with stepped or otherwise varied load so the target control is usable, controls_used is non-empty, and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps can be estimated.

hypotheses.observation: Pair-04, pair-11, and pair-12 carry status CANDIDATE with best_lag_rho values of -0.342830910072, -0.322225144351, and 0.330827674706 respectively, but their Holm-adjusted p-values are 0.686, 0.702, and 0.51 with reason HOLM_NOT_REJECTED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Within a family of 16 simultaneous hypotheses, these non-selected candidates are consistent with chance-level fluctuation and were not rejected at the family level.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Do not treat these candidates as load effects; keep them only as leads and re-examine their series if a subsequent load-varying run reproduces them.

hypotheses.observation: The resource binding reports clock_alignment "not_verified_by_core", and correlation pairs report best lags up to ±10000 ms (pair-14 best_lag_ms -10000).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment between the metric and resource telemetry feeds, an optimal lag value cannot support a lead/lag ordering or a temporal causal hypothesis.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization/alignment of the telemetry feeds before interpreting any best_lag_ms value as a timing relationship.

hypotheses.observation: The diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested 0, episodes_reported 0, pairs_evaluable 16, pairs_tested 16, status COMPLETE, and uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Zero anomalies tested and zero episodes reported reflect the diagnostic method run in this analysis, not proof that no resource-to-response relationship exists or that the service has spare capacity.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Base capacity reasoning on the selected candidate and on new load-varying runs rather than on the absence of reported episodes.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment between the JMeter metric telemetry and the service resource telemetry before interpreting any lagged correlation.
recommendations.rationale: The resource binding states clock_alignment "not_verified_by_core"; an unverified clock relationship cannot support lead/lag ordering or temporal causation, and several pairs, including the selected pair-14, have best lags at ±10000 ms.

recommendations.action: Configure an applicable business policy rule and/or a resource rule with effect: sla for the window, then rerun so the product can evaluate PASS or FAIL.
recommendations.rationale: Both windows report NO_POLICY for business and resource verdicts, and the deterministic verdict stays NO_POLICY until an applicable rule is evaluated; healthy metrics alone never turn NO_POLICY into PASS.

recommendations.action: Inspect the resource-14 series (and its neighbors in the same service group, e.g. resource-15) across the evaluation window and rerun to see whether the pair-14 negative lagged association reproduces.
recommendations.rationale: pair-14 is the only headline selected after Holm correction (adjusted p 0.016) and is reported as a correlation_candidate, but its uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED and its best lag is at the tested range boundary.

recommendations.action: Rerun the test with stepped or otherwise varied load instead of a constant 20 requests/s target.
recommendations.rationale: The target series is constant with 0 standard deviation, so every correlation pair dropped the target control (CONSTANT_CONTROL), leaving no load control, no controls_used, and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps null.

recommendations.action: Report the run outcome as NO_POLICY without interpreting zero errors, low latency, zero anomalies, or the absence of selected correlations as a pass or as proof of stability or spare capacity.
recommendations.rationale: NO_POLICY is deterministic and independent of how healthy the run looks; the anomaly diagnostic tested 0 episodes and all correlation uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED, so those absences have no evidentiary weight for stability or capacity.

caveats: The deterministic verdict NO_POLICY is preserved exactly; this advice does not change it and a rerun only yields PASS/FAIL if an applicable rule is evaluated.

Correlation pairs cover only the evaluation window (from_epoch_ms 1767225720000 to 1767225960000, 240 cells); the reference window and parts of the run outside these windows are not covered by correlation analysis.

Every correlation pair reports uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, controls dropped due to CONSTANT_CONTROL (constant 20 requests/s target), and null sensitivity_without_achieved_rps, so the statistical evidence is limited even for the selected pair-14.
Clock alignment between telemetry feeds is not verified by core, so best_lag_ms values cannot support lead/lag ordering or temporal causation.
The anomaly diagnostic reported anomalies_tested 0 and episodes_reported 0; this does not prove stability, spare capacity, low load, or absence of a problem.

Metric summaries are scoped to the overall run and one transaction label 'request' within sampled windows (7200 samples overall, 2400 reference, 4800 evaluation); counts are not comparable across scopes.
No capacity bound, capacity knee, or generator guard data is present in the referenced evidence; capacity limits and generator health were not assessed.
The current date context (October 7, 2026) is unrelated to the analysis timestamps (epochs around 1767225600000); no temporal relationship between them is asserted.
